A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete 19-page document, including Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments on ImageNet-LT, Places365-LT, and iNaturalist2018 in Tables 5–8, plus ablations, constructed-data experiments, and case studies in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results in Tables 5–8 and the additional empirical analyses in Appendix E, including the synthetic six-class experiment.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same backdoor-adjustment procedure, combining balanced predictions from CLIP, OpenCLIP, and MetaCLIP. The components, objectives, and inference procedure are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three classification benchmarks, constructed Places365 imbalance scenarios, and synthetic six-class dataset in Appendix E. No dataset, task, or evaluated scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within every corresponding experiment. Tables 5–7 retain their respective baseline rows, and the GLA variants, CE/LA comparisons, and decoupling comparison are unchanged.

E3.justification: The backbone configurations, training budgets, evaluation metrics, class-group definitions, and constructed-data procedures are identical. Appendix A and Table 9 retain the same experimental settings.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix E retain the same semantic-factor ablations, classifier analysis, imbalance scenarios, occlusion cases, visualizations, and synthetic confounding experiment. No analysis is added, removed, or revised.

E5.justification: Appendix E.4 reports averaging over three constructed datasets per scenario in both versions. Repetition information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged throughout.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and graphical findings match, including appendix results. Tables 5–7 retain overall accuracies of 53.01% on Places365-LT, 79.57% on ImageNet-LT, and 82.01% on iNaturalist2018.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, the logit-adjustment mathematics, the causal assumptions and backdoor derivation in Section 4, and appendix equations are identical. No formal reasoning or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion are identical. Claims about parameter imbalance, limitations of re-balancing, incomplete semantic confounding, and the proposed adjustment retain the same scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations of imbalance, classifier effects, and semantic confounding are unchanged. Appendix E.5 retains the same qualification that increasing the number of semantic factors raises computational costs.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures are identical, including Appendix A's learning rate, batch size, training epochs, and hardware. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The references, Section 6 related work, and Appendix C comparisons with earlier causal approaches are identical. No cited work or substantive research positioning changes.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2, dated 4 May 2025, to v3, dated 8 Aug 2025. This is a limited administrative text edit; body language, terminology, and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12, Tables 1–17, captions, and page layouts are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–19 match exactly; the only visible difference on page 1 is the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The complete scientific text, results, appendices, and visual presentation are identical. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp does not meaningfully affect the paper's clarity, rigor, reproducibility, or evidential support.
